opcoes.texto: The main cause was probably the paperwork.
The end of April is realistic.

exercicios.enunciado: Em certa medida, o atraso esteve fora do nosso controlo.
exercicios.resposta: To a certain extent, the delay was outside our control.

exercicios.frase: I'm Thandi. Clients tend to forgive delays. They don't forgive surprises.
exercicios.enunciado: What do clients not forgive, according to Thandi?

exercicios.frase: This is Thandi. Arguably, it is partly our fault. Nobody told them in writing.
exercicios.enunciado: Why is it partly Mopane's fault, according to Thandi?

opcoes.texto: Nobody told the client in writing.

exercicios.frase: It would appear that there was a problem with the paperwork.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com ritmo calmo.
A project went wrong. Explain to the people affected what happened and why, without blaming anyone and without hiding the facts. Use at least four hedging expressions.
exercicios.frase: It would appear
exercicios.resposta: The new system opened two weeks late, and I'm sorry. It would appear that the main problem was the old data: some of it seems to have been incomplete. To a certain extent, that was outside our control, but arguably we should have tested earlier.

exercicios.enunciado: In your culture, is it more polite to be direct or to soften what you say? Does it depend on the situation?
exercicios.frase: tend to
exercicios.resposta: In Angola, people tend to soften things with older people and with clients. With friends, we're much more direct. I'm inclined to think it depends more on the relationship than on the culture.

licoes.objectivo: Exprimir graus finos de certeza e de probabilidade.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'm [fairly] confident it'll be this week.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: It's [highly] unlikely that we'll finish before mid-April.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'd be surprised if it [took] more than ten days.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I wouldn't rule it [out].

exercicios.enunciado: Which expression shows the HIGHEST certainty?
Which expression shows the LOWEST probability?
"I'd be surprised if it cost more than five thousand." The speaker thinks it will probably cost…
"I wouldn't rule out a week or two more." This means a delay is…

opcoes.texto: possible, and we should be ready for it

exercicios.enunciado: Muito provavelmente, seis semanas.

exercicios.frase: I'm Inês. I'm fairly confident it'll be this week. Let's say eighty percent.
exercicios.enunciado: How sure is Inês that the containers will be released this week?

exercicios.frase: This is Bongani. It's highly unlikely we'll finish before mid-April. There's a slim chance, ten percent maybe.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Bongani think about finishing before mid-April?

exercicios.frase: I'm Inês. It's the rainy season in Nampula until April. If the roads flood, we lose a week or two.
exercicios.enunciado: Why might the project be delayed in Nampula?

exercicios.frase: I'm fairly confident. It's highly unlikely. There's a slim chance.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com o acento em "fairly", "highly" e "slim".
Talk about three things over the next year: one you're fairly confident about, one you wouldn't rule out, and one that's highly unlikely, with a reason for each.
exercicios.frase: highly unlikely
exercicios.resposta: I'm fairly confident I'll finish this course by December: I study every evening. I wouldn't rule out a move to another department. And it's highly unlikely that I'll buy a car this year. I'd be surprised if prices came down.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it better for a manager to give an optimistic estimate or a careful one? Why?
exercicios.frase: surprised
exercicios.resposta: A careful one. If you say April and deliver in March, people are happy. If you say March and deliver in April, they're angry. I'd be surprised if any client preferred a promise that wasn't kept.

licoes.titulo: We're not in a position to…
licoes.objectivo: Recusar e dar más notícias com diplomacia, propondo uma alternativa.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'm afraid we're not in a [position] to pay for that.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: I'm afraid that [falls] outside what we agreed.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: What we [can] do is accept the new date.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

We're not in position of paying.

exercicios.enunciado: A diplomatic refusal usually has…

opcoes.texto: a softener, the refusal, a reason and an alternative

exercicios.enunciado: "That's not ideal." In diplomatic English, this often means…
"Let me come back to you on that." The speaker…
Lamento, mas isso está fora do que acordámos.
exercicios.resposta: I'm afraid that falls outside what we agreed.

exercicios.frase: I'm Clare, from Halvorsen Radio. The last six radios will be two more weeks. We'd ask Mopane to cover the air freight.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Clare ask Mopane to do?

exercicios.frase: This is Nuno. I'm afraid that falls outside what we agreed. The contract says the warranty starts on installation.
exercicios.enunciado: When does the warranty start, according to the contract?

exercicios.frase: I'm afraid we're not in a position to pay for that.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com "I'm afraid" suave e descendente.
Someone important (a client, a manager or a relative) asks for something you can't give. Refuse with diplomacy, give the reason, and offer an alternative.
exercicios.frase: What I can do
exercicios.resposta: I really appreciate that you thought of me. But I'm afraid I'm not in a position to work this weekend: my daughter has an exam on Monday. What I can do is come in early on Monday and Tuesday.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it harder to say no to a client, to a manager or to a family member? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: To a family member, because there's no contract to hide behind. With a client, I can say it falls outside what we agreed. With family, it's personal, so I try to offer something else.

That was very gentil of you.

"In theory, yes…" said with a fall-rise tone suggests…

exercicios.frase: This is Ms Mahlangu, the director. It's been a challenging year, and I'm afraid the budget has been reduced. Going forward, we'll focus on the website.
exercicios.enunciado: What will the team focus on from now on?

exercicios.frase: In theory, yes…
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com a voz a descer e a subir no fim.
Announce bad news to a team: the budget has been cut and a project will stop. Be honest but gentle. Then say what it really means, in plain words.
exercicios.frase: not ideal
exercicios.resposta: It's been a challenging year, and I'm afraid the budget has been reduced, so the app project will stop. I know this isn't ideal. Going forward, we'll focus on the website. In plain words: less money, no app.

exercicios.enunciado: Does corporate language help people, or does it hide the truth? Give an example.
exercicios.frase: example
exercicios.resposta: Both. For example, "we're reviewing your proposal" protects feelings, but it can hide a no. I'm inclined to think it helps when the facts are also clear.

exercicios.enunciado: When does Achieng want the new version?

exercicios.frase: This is Tumelo. Full responsibility is a legal phrase. If they go to court, it's also an expensive phrase, and it isn't even true.
exercicios.enunciado: Why is "full responsibility" a problem, according to Tumelo?

opcoes.texto: It could be expensive in court, and it isn't fully true.

exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.
Choose one of the three calls. Tell a colleague what the caller really meant, what they didn't say, and what Nuno should do next.
exercicios.frase: really meant
exercicios.resposta: Achieng really meant that our price is too high, but the quality is good. What she didn't say is how much lower. She invited a new version before the twenty-eighth, so I'd lower the price a little and add something extra.

exercicios.enunciado: Would you prefer people to say "no" directly, or diplomatically? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: At work, diplomatically, because relationships last longer than one deal. But I'd like the no to be clear. A polite no is fine; a polite maybe that means no wastes everyone's time.

A client is angry: you delivered late, and they ask for a big discount and a guaranteed date. Acknowledge, explain with hedging, give an honest degree of certainty, refuse the discount with a reason, and offer something else.
exercicios.frase: I'm afraid
exercicios.resposta: You're right that we should have called you sooner, and I apologise. It would appear that the problem was our transport company. I'm fairly confident it'll arrive on Thursday. I'm afraid we can't offer fifty percent, but what we can do is free delivery on your next three orders.

exercicios.enunciado: Summarise this letter in English, in three or four sentences: "Manifesto o meu descontentamento com o serviço de limpeza do nosso escritório em Janeiro. Várias vezes, as salas não foram limpas. Caso não melhore até ao fim de Fevereiro, procuraremos outro fornecedor. Solicito uma reunião."
exercicios.frase: unhappy
exercicios.resposta: The client is unhappy with our cleaning service in January: several times, the rooms weren't cleaned. If things don't improve by the end of February, they'll look for another company. They're asking for a meeting as soon as possible.
exercicios.contexto: Mediação: o essencial, em inglês simples.

exercicios.enunciado: Give a client some bad news: a project will be three months late. Be honest, but keep the client.
exercicios.frase: apologise
exercicios.resposta: I'm afraid I have some difficult news: the project will be about three months late, and I apologise. It would appear that the main cause was our supplier. I'm reasonably confident about June. What I can offer is a weekly report and a free month of support.

exercicios.enunciado: A colleague asks: "Will the new system be ready on Monday?" You are about 30% sure. Answer honestly.
exercicios.frase: wouldn't
exercicios.resposta: Honestly, I wouldn't count on Monday. There's a fair chance, but I'd say it's somewhat unlikely. I'm fairly confident about Wednesday, and I'll confirm on Friday afternoon.
